name: Hatah
title: Queen Esther's Chamberlain
summary: Hatah (also known as Hatakh) was one of King Ahasuerus' chamberlains appointed to serve Queen Esther. He acted as a messenger between Esther and her foster father Mordecai during the critical period when the Jews were threatened by Haman's extermination plan. His faithful service as an intermediary was crucial for the communication that led to the salvation of the Jewish people.

keyEvents.title: Appointed to Serve Esther
keyEvents.description: Hatah was one of the king's chamberlains who was designated to serve Queen Esther personally at court.

keyEvents.title: Sent to Mordecai
keyEvents.description: When Esther heard that Mordecai was mourning in sackcloth and ashes, she sent Hatah out to find out what was wrong and why he was grieving.

keyEvents.title: Meeting with Mordecai at the City Square
keyEvents.description: Hatah went out to Mordecai on the open square before the king's gate to hear his message.

keyEvents.title: Received information about Haman's plan
keyEvents.description: Mordecai told Hatak everything that had happened to him, including the exact sum of money Haman had promised to pay into the king's treasury to have the Jews destroyed, and gave him a copy of the decree of destruction.

keyEvents.title: Messenger between Mordecai and Esther
keyEvents.description: Hatak brought Mordecai's message and a copy of the decree back to Esther, and then conveyed Esther's reply back to Mordecai, where she explained her fear of approaching the king uninvited.

keyEvents.title: Delivered Mordecai's crucial appeal
keyEvents.description: Hatak delivered Mordecai's famous call to action to Esther, reminding her that perhaps she had come to her royal position for such a time as this.
